family.d: a group of people like a mom, a dad, and their children. Families = more than one family.

work.d: to do a job; work = the things you do at a job. It also means to go well. "How does a family farm work?" = how the people on a farm do all the farm jobs.
work.ex: Mom works in a big office. My new toy car works well.

together.d: with each other, in one group.

farm.d: a place in the country where people grow food and keep animals.
farm.ex: We saw cows and pigs at the farm.

time345.d: a time very, very early in the morning. The sky is still dark. a.m. = in the morning.
time345.ex: At 3:45 a.m., I am asleep in bed.

tuesday.d: a day of the week. It comes after Monday.
tuesday.ex: I have art class on Tuesday.

mary.d: a name for a girl. In this story, Mary Gelder works on her family farm.
mary.ex: Mary sells fruit at the market.

gelder.d: a family name. The Gelders = Mary and her family. They live on a farm in Michigan.
gelder.ex: The Gelders work on their farm every day.

mom.ex: My mom reads to me at night.

drive.d: to make a car or truck go and move it on the road.
drive.ex: My dad drives me to school.

many.ex: There are many stars in the sky.

miles.d: a mile is a long way. Many miles = a very long way.
miles.ex: We drove many miles to see Grandma.

michigan.d: a big place in the north of the United States. It has many farms and very big lakes.
michigan.ex: Michigan has big lakes and apple farms.

chicago.d: a very big city in the United States, next to a big lake.

sell.d: to give something to a person, and the person gives you money for it.

fruit.d: sweet food that grows on trees and plants, like apples and bananas. Fruits = more than one fruit.

vegetables.d: plants we eat, like carrots, corn and potatoes.

farmer.d: a person who works on a farm. A farmer grows food or keeps animals.

market.d: a place where people buy and sell food and other things. Many markets are outside. At a farmer's market, farmers sell their food.
market.ex: We buy fresh corn at the farmer's market.

customers.d: people who buy things at a shop or a market.
customers.ex: The shop has many customers on Saturday.

visit.d: to go and see a person or a place.

stand.d: a small table or a little shop outside where people sell things.
stand.ex: The farm stand has apples and corn.

buy.d: to give money to get something. bought = the past of buy.

fresh.d: just picked or just made; not old.
fresh.ex: The bread is fresh and warm.

food.d: the things that people and animals eat.

see.d: to look at something with your eyes.
see.ex: I can see a bird in the tree.

eat.d: to put food in your mouth and chew it.

hard.d: with a lot of work; trying very much.
hard.ex: She works hard in the garden.

grow.d: to put plants in the ground and help them get bigger.
grow.ex: We grow tomatoes in our garden.

says.d: speaks words. says = he says / she says.

long.ex: It was a long day at the zoo.

day.d: the time when it is light outside.

return.d: to come back or go back.

home.ex: My home has a red door.

again.ex: Let's go down the slide again!

saturday.d: a day of the week. It comes after Friday. Many kids have no school on Saturday.

stop.d: to not move, or to not do something anymore.
stop.ex: The bus stops at the red light.

chores.d: small jobs you do at home, like making your bed or feeding your pet.
chores.ex: My chores are making my bed and feeding the cat.

plant.d: to put seeds or small plants in the ground so they can grow.

waters.d: gives water to plants. waters = he waters / she waters.
waters.ex: Grandpa waters the flowers every morning.

picks.d: takes a fruit or a flower off the plant with the hand.
picks.ex: She picks an apple from the tree.

jobs.d: work that a person does. Some jobs are work for money. Some jobs are work you do at home.
jobs.ex: A doctor and a cook have different jobs.

care.d: to look after someone or something and keep it safe and well.
care.ex: I take care of my puppy. I feed it every day.

chickens.d: farm birds. Chickens give us eggs.
chickens.ex: The chickens eat corn on the farm.

brothers.d: boys or men who have the same mom and dad as you.

repair.d: to fix something that is broken.

trucks.d: big cars that carry heavy things.
trucks.ex: The truck carries apples to the city.

tractors.d: big, strong farm trucks with very big wheels. They pull things in the fields.
tractors.ex: The farmer drives a green tractor.

check.d: to look at something carefully to see if it is OK.
check.ex: I check my bike tires before I ride.

tools.d: things you hold in your hand to help you do work, like a hammer or a saw.
tools.ex: Dad keeps his tools in a red box.

like.ex: Farms have animals, like cows and pigs.

shovels.d: tools with a long handle and a wide end. You use a shovel to dig.
shovels.ex: We dig a hole with a shovel.

drills.d: tools that make holes in wood or walls. The end turns very fast.
drills.ex: Mom uses a drill to make a hole.

rene.d: Mary's mom. René takes care of the farm money and the workers.
rene.ex: René says, "I'm proud of my family!"

money.d: coins and paper money. You use money to buy things.
money.ex: Money can buy food and toys.

workers.d: people who work at a job.
workers.ex: The workers build a new house.

choose.d: to pick one thing from many things.

look.d: to use your eyes to see something. a look = when you look at something.

demand.d: how much people want to buy something.
demand.ex: On hot days, there is a big demand for ice cream.

summer.d: the hot time of the year.

people.ex: Many people are at the park.

strawberries.d: small, red, sweet fruits with tiny seeds on the outside.

lot.ex: There are a lot of apples in the box.

sometimes.d: not always, but some of the time.
sometimes.ex: Sometimes I ride my bike to school.

less.ex: Sometimes we eat less than we have.

turn.d: to change something so it becomes something new.

extra.ex: I have an extra pencil. You can use it.

jam.d: a sweet food made from cooked fruit and sugar. You put it on bread.
jam.ex: I eat bread with strawberry jam.

winter.d: the cold time of the year.

supply.d: the things you have and can use, ready for later.
supply.ex: We have a big supply of snacks for the trip.

produce.d: to make or grow things, often to sell them. produced = the past of produce.

consume.ex: Our family consumes a lot of milk.

items.d: things. One thing is an item.
items.ex: There are five items in my lunch box.

called.d: having this name. "are called consumers" = their name is consumers.

consumers.d: people who buy and use things.
consumers.ex: Kids are consumers when they buy toys.

bicycle.d: a bike. It has two wheels, and you push the pedals with your feet.
bicycle.ex: I ride my bicycle in the park.

kids.ex: The kids play on the swings.

athletes.d: people who are very good at sports and play sports a lot.
athletes.ex: The athletes run in a race.

books.d: things you read. Books have pages with words and pictures.

teachers.d: a person who helps students learn at school.
teachers.ex: My teacher reads us a story.

students.ex: The students sit at their desks.

readers.ex: My sister is a good reader.

animals.d: living things like dogs, cats, birds and fish.
animals.ex: We saw many animals at the zoo.

cars.d: things with four wheels that people drive on the road.
cars.ex: There are many cars on the road.

drivers.d: people who drive cars, buses or trucks.

apples.d: round red or green fruits that grow on trees.
apples.ex: I eat an apple every day.

other.ex: One shoe is red. The other shoe is blue.

running.d: running a farm = being the boss of a farm and making all the work happen.
running.ex: Mom is running a small bakery.

cost.d: to need this much money to buy it. "costs five dollars" = you must pay five dollars to get it.
cost.ex: This toy car costs five dollars.

try.d: to do your best to do something.
try.ex: I try to tie my shoes.

save.d: to keep money and not use it now.
save.ex: I save my coins in a piggy bank.

ago.ex: Some time ago, I was a baby.

wood.d: the hard part of a tree. We use it for fires, tables and houses.
wood.ex: Dad puts wood on the fire.

stove.d: a metal box that gets very hot. Some stoves cook food. Some stoves burn wood to make a home warm.
stove.ex: The wood stove keeps our house warm.

burn.d: to make fire with something. Fire burns wood.
burn.ex: We burn wood in the campfire.

trees.d: tall plants with a hard, woody stem and many leaves.

heat.d: the hot feeling from a fire or the sun.
heat.ex: The heat from the fire keeps us warm.

warms.d: makes something a little hot. warms = it warms.

barn.d: a big farm building for animals, food for animals and tools.
barn.ex: The cows sleep in the barn.

help.d: to do something good for someone so it is easier for them. helped = the past of help.
help.ex: I help my dad wash the car.

spend.d: to use money to buy things.
spend.ex: I spend my money on books.

cold.d: not warm; like ice and snow.

months.d: a year has twelve months, like January and May.

environment.d: the air, water, land, plants and animals all around us.

proud.d: happy about something good that you or your family did.
proud.ex: I am proud of my drawing.

around.d: look around = look at all the things near you, on every side.
around.ex: Look around the room. What do you see?

things.d: anything you can see and hold, like toys, cups and books.
things.ex: Put your things in your bag.

make.d: to build something or put things together, so you have something new. made = the past of make.
make.ex: I made a card for Mom.

person.d: one man, one woman or one child.
person.ex: One person sits on the bench.

goods.d: things that people make or grow to sell, like toys, shoes and food.

provide.d: to give people something they need.
provide.ex: The school provides lunch for us.

offer.d: to say you will give or do something for someone.
offer.ex: I offer my friend a cookie.

services.d: work that a person does to help other people, like cutting hair or teaching. Services = more than one service.

actions.d: things that you do, like jump, run or clap.

police.d: a person whose job is to keep people safe.
police.ex: The police officer helps us cross the street.

firefighters.d: people whose job is to stop fires and help people.
firefighters.ex: The firefighters put out the fire.

factories.d: big buildings where people and big tools make many things.

include.d: to have as one part of a group.
include.ex: My favorite fruits include apples and grapes.

server.d: a person who brings food to your table at a restaurant.
server.ex: The food server brings us pizza.

learn.d: to get to know something new.

brings.d: carries something to a person or place. brings = he brings / she brings.
brings.ex: My dog brings me the ball.

table.d: a thing with a flat top and legs. You eat or work at a table.

restaurant.d: a place where you pay to eat a meal.
restaurant.ex: We eat at a restaurant on my birthday.

earn.d: to get money for your work.
earn.ex: I earn money when I wash Dad's car.

use.d: to do something with a thing.
use.ex: I use a spoon to eat soup.

live.d: to be alive. People need food and water to live.

needs.d: things you must have to live, like food, water, a home and clothes.

clothing.d: clothes; things you wear, like shirts and pants.
clothing.ex: Put on warm clothing in winter.

wish.ex: I wish for a new bike.

wants.d: things you would like to have, but you do not need them to live, like toys and games.

games.d: things you play for fun, like board games and ball games.

create.ex: We create a robot from boxes.

choice.d: when you pick one thing; the thing you pick.
choice.ex: The choice is yours: an apple or a banana?

more.ex: Can I have more milk, please?

do.d: to make an action happen. do chores = clean, cook, wash and so on.
do.ex: I do my homework after school.

such.ex: I like sports, such as soccer and swimming.

old.d: not new; it has been here a long time.
old.ex: My grandpa has an old car.

eachother.d: one another. We help each other = I help you and you help me.
eachother.ex: My sister and I help each other.

others.ex: It is good to help others.
